item.title: 8.000 personas se han apuntado para ayudar en una reforma de Japón: están moviendo un castillo de 360 toneladas con una cuerda
item.description: En Hirosaki, al norte de Japón, una compleja restauración patrimonial se ha convertido en algo bastante más insólito: miles de personas tirando de cuerdas para desplazar un castillo de cientos de toneladas. La operación utiliza una antigua técnica japonesa que permite trasladar edificios completos sin desmontarlos y ha despertado tal interés que las plazas disponibles se quedaron pequeñas. Detrás del espectáculo hay una historia que comenzó con un terremoto . Japón pidió voluntarios. El ayuntamiento de Hirosaki necesitaba voluntarios para una operación bastante difícil de encontrar en… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: In the late 1920s, mule deer were brought to Catalina Island; now a judge has ordered for 2,000 of them to be culled
item.description: Catalina Island's mule deer, released in the late 1920s, now pose serious threats to local flora and contribute to increased wildfire risks. In response, conservation leaders have outlined a contentious strategy to significantly reduce the mule deer population. Following a legal challenge that was dismissed by a judge, the cull is set to commence, aimed at preserving the island's natural environment and lowering fire hazards. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Chinese man, Nepali woman found alive 10 days after flood
item.description: Rescuers pulled out a 64-year-old Nepali woman alive on Saturday from her home, buried under thick mud and debris when the region was struck by massive flooding 10 days ago, killing over 1,300 people and leaving at least 5,500 missing. Emergency personnel said earlier they had rescued a Chinese man, named only as Luhaitao, found alive inside a 225-metre tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal’s Rasuwa district. Footage ‌shared by the Nepali army showed him being given... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Reform continues to cast doubt on climate science. Do its supporters agree?
item.description: Climate scepticism is common at the Reform party conference, but many also criticise Labour for failing to protect Britons from hot weather On the second day of the Reform UK conference, in the wake of an undercover investigation alleging party officials plotted to evade the law on foreign donations, the deputy leader, Richard Tice, addressed the audience. Within minutes, a banner appeared behind him reading: “Collect £5m, burn the planet.” It was taken down promptly and Tice, who has repeatedly called on people to enjoy the summer’s five successive heatwaves and record drought , rolled on… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: A Texas teenager started building birdhouses after losing his pet cockatiel; now he has inspired a conservation movement across 20 states
item.description: After adopting a pet cockatiel, Aamir Tinwala initiated a bird conservation movement focused on building birdhouses to combat habitat loss. His project promotes awareness of local biodiversity while encouraging community members to take an active role in habitat stewardship. Tinwala has personally constructed over 750 shelters and inspired countless others, illustrating how individual efforts can lead to significant environmental benefits. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In 2016, Florida’s living shorelines withstood Hurricane Matthew’s 90 mph winds intact
item.description: A living shoreline project in New Smyrna Beach largely survived Hurricane Matthew's severe winds. This natural approach used vegetation and sand to stabilize the coast effectively. Conventional hardened structures nearby experienced significant damage and erosion during the storm. The project demonstrated how natural defenses can withstand powerful hurricane conditions. This resilience offers a promising model for future coastal protection strategies. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why are they killing this beautiful fish?
item.description: Lionfish are beautiful, venomous and devastating Caribbean reefs. In Honduras, divers are fighting back with homemade spears, hunting competitions and by putting lionfish on restaurant menus. Watch the full film to meet the community fighting back against one of the Caribbean’s most destructive invasive species. Fuente: Mongabay.

item.description: Insurers in England and Wales tell of busy August with one reporting near-140% jump in claims UK insurers are experiencing a surge in the number of homeowners making claims for subsidence after the hottest summer on record , with Hastings Direct reporting a near 140% jump to an all-time high for August. item.title: Typhoon Saudel: days of flooding trigger fatal landslide in central China
item.description: At least one person was killed and 11 are missing after they were buried by a landslide in central China as the region continued to battle severe flooding caused by Typhoon Saudel. The landslide hit Gaoping, a town in a mountainous area of Jiangxi province, at around 4am on Saturday, according to state broadcaster CCTV. It said rescue teams were rushing to the disaster site. The accident followed days of torrential rain brought by the outer bands of Typhoon Saudel and a cold front. Floodwaters... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Country diary: The wild, riotous sounds of otters in battle | Cal Flyn
item.description: Isle of Lismore, Argyll: They skim over the surface like stones, making such a hullabaloo you could hear them a mile away I hear them before I see them: a wailing, or something more like ululation. High-pitched, repeated vocalisations that are neither man nor cat, but somewhere in between. I throw open the cabin door, unsure what to look for, and for a moment see nothing new: only the rocky strand and the sweep of dark wrack high above the shoreline. The strange, warbling sound comes again. Ai-ai-ai-ai. Not quite screaming, not quite howling, not quite trilling, but all of those things at… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Cal Flyn

item.title: Trump order directs officials to consider stripping protections for gray wolves
item.description: Interior department given three months to decide whether wolves can be removed from endangered species list Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday directing the interior department to consider de-listing gray wolves from the Endangered Species Act and to contemplate whether the agency could make it easier to authorize killing them. The order gives interior secretary Doug Burgum three months to determine whether gray wolves and Mexican gray wolves have recovered enough for the federal government to de-list them. item.title: ONU alerta sobre potencia que tendrá fenómeno de El Niño en el mundo
item.description: La ONU alertó que el fenómeno de El Niño será de una categoría muy fuerte y existe la posibilidad de que incluso sea un evento de categoría excepcionalmente fuerte, superando las escalas de medición usadas en las últimas cuatro décadas. El fenómeno natural puede generar tifones, inundaciones y sequías severas en varias partes del mundo, que, según los científicos, cada vez son más potentes por el impacto del cambio climático. item.description: Nepal's emergency crews have pulled two workers out of a hydropower tunnel where they had been trapped for nine days. item.description: El cambio climático , el calor y la sequía no solo traen de cabeza a España. item.title: Record European fires burn over 500,000 hectares during summer
item.description: A record-breaking summer that saw more than 1,000 wildfires has torched some 540,000 hectares (1.3 million acres) of land across the European Union since mid-June, according to official data—an area more than twice the size of Luxembourg. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Since the 1980s, climate change has increasingly altered European bumblebee habitats
item.description: Global biodiversity loss is occurring at a rapid pace, driven by multiple human-caused factors, including overexploitation, pollution, invasive species and climate change. Despite increasing research on the impact of climate change on wildlife, few studies have formally attributed observed biodiversity declines to climate change or quantified its contribution relative to other factors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: France announces €1 billion aid for farmers after climate-hit summer
item.description: France has recorded its hottest summer on record this year as the country battled heatwaves, drought and massive wildfires. The extreme weather has continued into September, with France's national weather service placing five departments on orange alert for several days. Temperatures are expected to reach 40°C in some areas. France's agriculture minister also announced a plan to unlock over 1 billion euros in aid to the agriculture sector, which has been severely affected by the extreme weather. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Extreme drought now covers 44% of Puerto Rico
item.description: Puerto Rico’s normally rainy season has instead brought a severe and fast-growing drought. By August 25, three-quarters of the territory was in at least moderate drought, with extreme drought covering 44 percent and some areas receiving less than 20 percent of their usual rainfall. Water shortages have forced rationing, while farmers are losing crops and ranchers are running low on hay. The situation has become serious enough to trigger both local and federal disaster declarations. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
